title: Another Leg Up In US Inflation?
text:
Another Leg Up In US Inflation?

Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 15 Oct 2026

US inflation accelerated in September, with the headline consumer price index rising 3.7% year-on-year, up from 3.4% in August. This was hardly surprising given elevated energy prices, which were bound to feed through to consumer prices (see No Good Outcomes For Energy Inflation). Looking ahead, geopolitics and energy prices will, of course, remain key swing factors for inflation. But beyond energy, the question for investors and policymakers is whether price pressures will spread through the economy, pushing up long-term inflation expectations, as some Federal Reserve officials fear. Two scenarios are worth considering.First, US inflation moves higher in the coming months, but long-term survey and market-based inflation expectations remain well anchored. This is the status quo, and it is likely to persist as long as rising inflation is largely driven by energy supply disruptions and markets remain confident in the Fed’s commitment to its inflation target. The disruption could prove temporary, whether because of peace deals or adjustments in supply chains and demand. Meanwhile, real borrowing costs in the US have risen across the board this year, increasing the risk of an economic slowdown. The widening of US high-yield corporate credit spreads, and perhaps yesterday’s -15% plunge in CoreWeave’s share price, point to growing financial strains. If energy prices and/or economic growth moderate, the rise in US inflation will likely be short-lived.
